description: The pick-list. Each panel declares what it REQUIRES, so a method can be checked for feasibility before any data is read. Each also declares its FAMILIARITY, so a method can be ordered to earn its conclusions: conventional views first, in the form practitioners already read, then the views that ask for new thinking.

familiarity_ladder.conventional: A view any mass spectrometrist reads without explanation. This is where geometry-based selection gets checked against the frame people already trust.
familiarity_ladder.bridge: Familiar axes, unfamiliar emphasis. Readable on sight, but makes a point the usual output does not.
familiarity_ladder.novel: Asks the reader to accept a new way of seeing. Only lands once the conventional panels have already agreed.

panels.title: MS/MS head-to-tail vs Atlas library
panels.notes: The load-bearing panel. b ions blue, y ions red, unassigned grey, shared m/z axis, dot product on sqrt intensities, ppm per matched peak. If the geometry-selected identification is right, this is where it shows in a form nobody has to be taught.

panels.title: MS1 isotope envelope
panels.notes: Observed envelope with the expected averagine pattern overlaid, spacing annotated as 1.00335/z. Charge state confirmation the way people already confirm it.

panels.title: Extracted ion chromatogram
panels.notes: Peak shape at the ion's own m/z, extraction window stated. A real peak over >=2 consecutive scans is the thing the proximity tier claims; this shows whether it looks like one.

panels.title: Intensity vs retention time
panels.notes: Always valid. Log y: intensity spans five orders of magnitude in real cohorts.

panels.title: SeqStart vs intensity
panels.notes: Primary cluster only (cluster_rank 1); pooling clusters corrupts the pattern. Y is a per-protein choice: within-protein max for stable proteins, absolute log where a real anomaly must stay visible.

panels.title: Top3avg percentile across samples
panels.notes: Percentile, not rank. A densely packed distribution moves a protein several rank positions on measurement noise alone.

panels.title: Drift vs retention time
panels.notes: Blank for DDA (drift null). EXCLUDED for SONAR: its drift column is a quadrupole window position, not a drift time.

panels.title: m/z vs drift
panels.notes: Density/hexbin, not scatter: this is where ion count bites hardest. The trend line against m/z is the drift-offset regression, so this panel is also a calibration check.

panels.title: Protein stoichiometry ratios
panels.notes: Ratios only within one run. Carries n_peptides_used on both sides: a 1-peptide vs 3-peptide ratio is not the same measurement.

panels.title: Flux across runs
panels.notes: Needs a stated normalization. Raw Top3avg across runs mixes biology with loading.

panels.title: Ion flight (animated 3-D)

degrades_without.to: 2-D: m/z against RT, mobility axis collapsed

panels.notes: Replay of the event track. Earns its place only after the conventional panels have agreed on the same ions.

panels.title: Ion map to sample class
panels.notes: The HeLa/K562 question. Holds out by batch, never randomly: a random split lets the model read instrument and loading instead of cell line.

panels.title: Forensic track of one ion
panels.notes: The event ledger as a timeline, with coordinate at each hop. Same data the flight animation replays.
